verdict.rationale: NVIDIA documents official SDKs for programming its data center GPUs. These include the CUDA Toolkit (C++ and Python tile kernels), the HPC SDK compilers, CUDA-X libraries like cuML and cuDF, and the NVIDIA AI Enterprise/NIM software bundled with H200 NVL. Together they give a first-party development environment to build against. Missing for 10: an explicit statement in the SDK docs that these versions support the H200, and independent or hands-on corroboration of building against these SDKs on H200 hardware.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The NVIDIA® CUDA® Toolkit provides a development environment for creating high-performance, GPU-accelerated applications.
It is built on top of the CUDA Tile IR specification and allows you to write tile kernels in Python.
The NVIDIA HPC SDK C, C++, and Fortran compilers support GPU acceleration of HPC modeling and simulation applications with standard C++ and Fortran, OpenACC® directives, and CUDA®.
cuML includes an API (cuml.accel) that can run your existing scikit-learn, UMAP, or HDBSCAN code on GPUs with no code modifications.
NVIDIA AI Enterprise includes NVIDIA NIM™, a set of easy-to-use microservices designed to speed up enterprise generative AI deployment.
